request.question: What would SAP alone have missed?

answer:
**SAP alone would miss 76% of fleet downtime, all early-warning signals for failures, and USD 177M of lost revenue—because it cannot see operational data until a human raises a notification.**

The table below contrasts SAP-only visibility with the full picture when Snowflake adds operational systems:

| Metric | SAP alone | With operational data | Gap |
|--------|-----------|----------------------|-----|
| **Fleet downtime visible** | 24.2% of down-hours (only logged notifications) | 100% (24,468 down-hours from FMS) | Misses **76%** of downtime |
| **Warning before failure** | 0 days (learns on notification) | 7.3 days average (74/74 failures flagged HIGH pre-notification) | No predictive capability |
| **Lost tonnes** | 1.63 Mt | 6.73 Mt (worth **USD 177M** revenue) | Underestimates by **5.1 Mt** |
| **C1 cost per tonne** | Not available (cost ÷ ? tonnes) | **USD 21.33/t**, Q1 FY2027 | Cannot calculate |
| **Trucks at high risk today** | Not available (no sensors) | **8 trucks** at risk | Blind to imminent failures |
| **Revenue at risk (supplier)** | Spend only (8 materials) | **USD 5.45M/day** (linked to trucks & tonnes) | Cannot quantify operational impact |

**Next step:** Schedule predictive maintenance on the 8 high-risk trucks this week to avoid unplanned downtime and protect the remaining Q2 production target.

---

**Sources** *(simulated data for a fictional operator)*  
**OPS** (fleet telemetry, FMS, historian): Fleet availability, trucks at risk, downtime hours, failure warnings  
**MIXED** (SAP BDC · MaintenanceNotification + Operations): Downtime visibility, failure warnings, lost tonnes, C1 cost, revenue at risk  
**SAP_STANDIN** (cost postings): C1 cost denominator
